What is the relationship between the surface area of a molecule and the van der Waals force?
questions.a: The larger the surface area, the stronger the van der Waals force

questions.q: Which properties of substances are related to van der Waals forces? Explain how.
questions.a: Melting point and boiling point: the larger the van der Waals forces, the higher the boiling point of a substance. Branching of molecules: substances with more branches have a relatively smaller surface area, so weaker van der Waals forces

questions.q: Water is a small molecule. You would expect its van der Waals forces to be smaller than those of, for example, ethanol. Why is the boiling point of water still higher?
questions.a: This is because of the many hydrogen bonds in water

questions.q: Why is alcohol a liquid at room temperature and the heavier butane is not?
questions.a: Alcohol can form hydrogen bonds and butane cannot

questions.q: Which property do no molecular substances have, that salts and metals do have?
questions.a: Molecular substances do not conduct electric current

questions.q: Describe molecular lattice
questions.a: A regular arrangement of molecules when the substance is in the solid state.
